lede: The one topic Tuesday's feeds agreed on was open-source AI image tooling: Comfy-Org/ComfyUI was trending on GitHub at the same time a Comfy-tuned model, flux-3-image-klein-comfy, climbed Hugging Face's trending list. Everything louder than that was gaming. Counter-Strike 2 peaked at 1,180,247 concurrent players on Steam, and Call of Duty surfaced across Steam, Twitch and Wikipedia on the same morning. The biggest single number on the board belonged to YouTube, where a stunt video titled 'If You Escape, You Win $1,000,000' reached 8,818,909 views.

throughlines.title: Comfy-Org/ComfyUI
throughlines.gist: The open-source engine for AI image generation turned up on GitHub trending while a Comfy-compatible model trended on Hugging Face, a rare case of a builder tool and its output moving together.

throughlines.title: Call of Duty
throughlines.gist: The franchise showed up at once on Steam, Twitch and Wikipedia, the kind of three-way overlap that marks a title people are playing, watching and reading about on the same day.

throughlines.title: Grand Theft Auto V Legacy
throughlines.gist: More than a decade after release, the game still bridged feeds, holding its place on Steam while resurfacing in YouTube's trending videos.
